title: Isaiah: the Holy One who comforts

lines: Isaiah spoke to the kings of Judah in the days of the Assyrian empire. His signature name for God comes from a vision: the Holy One of Israel.
Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.
Holiness exposes human pride. It also means God's commitment to his people.

scripture.text: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.

lines: The book has three major parts. The first speaks to Judah in the prophet's own day: judgment, threaded with promise.
From chapter forty, the voice speaks comfort to a people in exile. And the last chapters speak to a community back in the land, still waiting.

scripture.text: “Comfort, comfort My people,” says your God.

lines: Again and again the kings of Judah have to choose between trusting God and trusting military power or foreign alliances. Ahaz chooses Assyria. Hezekiah prays.
The book's verdict is that faith is the only real security.

scripture.text: If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all.

chapters.kicker: Watch for: judgment, and what is left
lines: God's judgment in Isaiah is real and severe, and it falls on Judah and on every nation alike. But it isn't where the book ends.
Through it God preserves a remnant, a people who will return to him.

scripture.text: Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the king and the Servant
lines: Isaiah gives three portraits of the one through whom God will act. A royal child from David's line. A Servant who suffers for others. And an anointed messenger of good news.
But He was pierced for our transgressions.
Jewish interpreters have often read the Servant as Israel. The New Testament sees all three in Jesus.

scripture.text: But He was pierced for our transgressions

chapters.kicker: Watch for: a world made new
lines: Isaiah sees Zion becoming the place where all nations come to learn God's ways. Israel's calling turns out to be for the sake of the whole world.
And the last chapters reach beyond Israel's history to new heavens and a new earth.

scripture.text: For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth.

lines: Isaiah is mostly poetry. Keep three horizons in view: the prophet's own day, the exile and return, and the far future.
The key chapters are one, six, seven, nine, thirty-seven, forty, fifty-three, and sixty-five.
Empires in this book come and go. One thing doesn't.
The word of our God stands forever.

scripture.text: the word of our God stands forever.
